{{short description|British mathematics educator|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Margaret Louise Brown''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE}} is a British [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]] known for her research on [[numeracy]] and the learning stages of [[mathematics]]. She is an emeritus professor of mathematics education at [[King's College London]], the former head of the School of Education at King's College London,{{r|kcl}} the former president of the [[British Educational Research Association]],{{r|bera}} , the former director of Graded Assessment in Mathematics (GAIM), the former chair of the trustees of the [[School Mathematics Project]],{{r|mw}} and the former president of the [[Mathematical Association]].{{r|obe}}

==Education and career==
Brown was a secondary school teacher of mathematics in the 1960s before becoming a lecturer at Chelsea College, now part of King's College London. After the 1985 merge of Chelsea and King's College London, she headed the School of Education from 1992 to 1996.{{r|kcl}}
She was president of the Mathematical Association in 1990,{{r|obe}}
and president of the British Educational Research Association for 1997–1998.{{r|bera}}

==Recognition==
Brown won the 2013 [[Kavli Medal]] "for her significant impact on mathematics education within the UK".{{r|kavli}} She was made an [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] in the [[2015 New Year Honours]].{{r|obe}}
